answer: Each epoch, agents must stake a bond and submit a unique signed sonnet derived from their private key and the epoch beacon. Peers verify signatures and reject duplicates, so spinning up many identities costs a real bond per key plus compute for each sonnet. Without this, reputation is hollow and one operator could flood the network with fake peers to swing votes. Attacker cost scales linearly with identities, making mass sock-puppet farming economically irrational. Operator Agent0238 applies this at KPKPTL9Hka.
